one_line: Earthworks beside an unpaved road on the Salar de Arizaro margin: scraped pad, spoil and a pit/loop visible in 2023 high-res imagery, absent in 2021.
summary: before.png (median of 2021-05 to 2022-03) shows uniform brown bare ground with only a faint unpaved track crossing the yellow box, about 100 m west of the pale evaporite margin of Salar de Arizaro; after.png (2023-05/06) shows a pale blotch filling the box east of the track, a second blotch just north-east, a third small bright spot about 200 m south-west at a track junction, and a sharper road. hires.png (Esri/WV03, 2023-07-21, 13 months after onset) resolves the box as a scraped patch of pale disturbed ground on the east shoulder of OSM way 241543244 with a spoil tail along the road, a pale rectangular pad with a dark object at its corner to the north-east, and a roughly 100 m pale-rimmed oval depression or turning loop abutting the box; wayback_strip.png shows none of this in the 2014, 2016, 2019 and 2021-10-13 releases and all of it in the 2023-10-11 and 2026-08-05 releases, bracketing the Sentinel-2 onset. The spectra are those of freshly exposed dry pale subsoil (d_brightness +0.049, d_swir +0.058, d_ndvi -0.004, d_nbr +0.029), the footprint brightened while the surrounding salt crust darkened (difference.png), and the step persists for four years with 12 of 12 later scenes agreeing and Landsat confirming; the 2022-06-07 scene is a dark anomalous acquisition shared by footprint and ring in timeseries.png, so the clean onset bracket is 2022-05-05 to 2022-07-19. All three sceptics (human activity, natural processes, artefacts) independently refuted the candidate with high confidence on the same evidence, differing only in how they describe the geometry of the pit versus pad outside the box. The panel concludes the change is ordinary mechanical earthworks beside an existing road in an active mining and exploration district (three OSM landuse=industrial polygons 2.0 to 2.4 km away; Lindero and Rio Grande mines 11 to 13 km), most likely an exploration or borrow working; the exact purpose is inferred, the earthwork itself is directly seen.
explanation: Ordinary earthworks on the east shoulder of an existing unpaved road (OSM way 241543244) at the western margin of Salar de Arizaro: a scraped or graded patch with spoil inside the footprint, plus an adjoining pale rectangular pad and a roughly 100 m pale-rimmed oval depression or turning loop just north-east of the box, all connected by vehicle tracks. Directly visible in hires.png (WV03, 2023-07-21) and in the Esri Wayback 2023-10-11 and 2026-08-05 releases, absent in the 2021-10-13 release; consistent with mineral or brine exploration pad/sump work or road-maintenance borrow in an active mining district. The precise purpose is inferred; the mechanical disturbance is seen.
next_step: A dated sub-metre image from the onset bracket (Planet or Maxar archive, 2022-05-05 to 2022-07-19) showing machinery, fresh spoil or a drill rig at -25.1072, -67.6410; or a Salta provincial mining cadastre lookup for exploration permits or drilling notices on the west shore of Salar de Arizaro near Vega Chascha in 2022, naming the operator of the three landuse=industrial sites 2 km away. Either would convert the inferred purpose into a documented one; the earthwork itself needs no further confirmation.
